tree.n: Take the center and open lines for your queen and bishop.

c.n: Develop and attack e5 right away.
Black defends e5.
The Italian bishop. It aims at f7, Black's weakest square.
Giuoco Piano. Black copies you.
Prepares a later d4 push.
Black attacks e4.
Calm. Protects e4 and keeps your position solid.
Black castles before playing ...d6.
Same setup as the main line. Next: a4, h3 and Nbd2–f1–g3.
King safety first.
Supports e4 and frees f1 for the knight's trip Nbd2–f1–g3.
Black makes room for ...Ba7 and eyes ...b5.
Stops ...b5 from chasing your bishop.
Takes g4 away from Black's bishop. Next: Nbd2–f1–g3.
Black hits your bishop and e4 at the same time.
Take. Otherwise ...dxc4 or ...dxe4 gives Black the center.
Two Knights Defense. Black attacks e4 instead of copying you.
Protect e4 calmly. You skip the wild 4.Ng5 lines.
Black heads for a Giuoco Piano setup.
Same plan: c3 prepares d4.
You reached the Giuoco Pianissimo by a different move order.
Supports e4 and frees f1 for the knight.
Prepares d4 later. Same slow plan as the Giuoco Piano.
Hungarian Defense. Solid but passive.
Black is passive, so grab the center at once.
Take back with the knight. You have more space.
Easy development and more space for you.
Black holds e5.
Develop and keep the tension.
A trap. If 4.Nxe5?? Qg5! hits your knight and g2, and Black wins.
Just trade knights.
Castle. Black wasted time and has a loose pawn on d4. Next: c3 to open lines.
The Ruy Lopez. You pressure the knight that defends e5.
Berlin Defense. Black attacks e4 at once.
Protect e4 and skip the famous Berlin endgame.
Prepares d4, which would hit the bishop on c5.
Stops ...Bg4. Next: Nbd2, Re1 and a slow build-up.
Black holds e5 with a pawn.
Same plan: c3, Re1, Nbd2–f1–g3, then d4 when ready.
Morphy Defense. Black asks the bishop what it wants.
Keep the bishop and the pressure.
Castle. e4 looks loose, but if ...Nxe4 you win it back with d4 or Re1.
Now e4 is safe, and Bxc6 followed by Nxe5 is a real threat.
Black kicks the bishop.
The bishop still aims at f7.
Black castles and hints at the Marshall Gambit (8.c3 d5!?).
Avoids the sharpest Marshall lines. After ...d6 you play c3 and reach the main line.
Back in the main line. Next: d4.
Prepares d4 and gives the bishop a retreat on c2.
Stops ...Bg4. Next: d4 with a big center.
The Open Ruy Lopez. Black takes the pawn.
Open the center while Black's king is still in the middle.
Black gives the pawn back to keep the knight on e4.
Gives your bishop a home on c2 and supports the center. Next: Nbd2 to challenge the e4 knight.
Black holds e5 with a pawn.
Prepares d4. Avoid 5.d4?! b5 6.Bb3 Nxd4, which can lead to the Noah's Ark trap where ...c5 and ...c4 trap your bishop.
Now take the center.
Castle. Next: Re1 and Nbd2.
Classical Defense. The bishop eyes f2.
Prepares d4, which will hit the bishop.
Take the center with tempo.
Protects e4 and keeps your center strong.
Schliemann Gambit. Black attacks e4 with a pawn.
Calm and safe. Keep the center solid.
